title: Transport guardrails: connection pool & timeout guidance across SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement conservative, production-safe transport defaults and example code across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that reduce connection churn, avoid head-of-line latency, and make streaming ergonomics robust. Goals: 1) Provide recommended presets for keep-alive, max connections, and per-route deadlines that map to common Redwood SLOs (low-latency interactive vs bulk/throughput). 2) Add opt-out compatibility path and migration notes so existing customers are not broken. 3) Ship cross-language examples and unit/integration tests validating behavior under dropped connections and slow backends. 4) Surface telemetry events to detect misconfigured clients (e.g., very short deadlines, excessive reconnects).
acceptance_criteria: Presets documented in SDK READMEs and in central transport guide (confluence) for interactive and throughput profiles
Python, TS, and Go SDKs implement new default presets behind feature flag with identical semantics
E2E test that simulates backend stall and verifies per-route deadline fallback and reconnect backoff behavior
Migration doc and changelog entry explaining opt-out and recommended tuning steps
Telemetry counters/metrics added to capture reconnection rate, pool exhaustion events, and per-request deadline truncation
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after cross-team sync. Observed customer reports of high token latencies correlated with aggressive client-side short deadlines and frequent TCP reconnects. Drafted goals and scope.

2026-03-11 - Marcus Chen: Scoped to core transport primitives only (no higher-level retry policy changes). Plan: implement presets + feature flag; add example snippets for all three languages; add integration test harness using local proxy to simulate network conditions.
2026-03-12 - Design review (Lena Ortiz): Request to include UX note for Console docs linking to per-route breakdowns so customers can correlate SDK tuning with observed throttle/reconnect telemetry.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Chen: Decided on two presets: interactive (SLO: 95% requests < 200ms tail) and throughput (SLO: maximize concurrency with pooled keepalive). Interactive defaults: keepalive=30s, max_conns_per_host=6, idle_conn_timeout=60s, default_deadline=60s. Throughput defaults: keepalive=15s, max_conns_per_host=24, idle_conn_timeout=120s, default_deadline=300s. These will be configurable via client options.

2026-03-13 - Engineering note: To avoid accidental breaking changes we will ship behind a feature flag 'transport_defaults_v2' enabling a gradual rollout. Add deprecation warning if customers explicitly set older values.

2026-03-13 - Test plan update (Sanjay Rao): Integration harness will use 'toxiproxy' to simulate TCP pause/resume, packet drops and RSTs; assert that SDK backoff + pool pruning avoids hot-loop reconnects and that streaming reconnects resume with exponential backoff and jitter.

2026-03-14 - Marcus Chen: WIP PR created for Python SDK implementing option struct and presets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/412. Waiting on TS/Go maintainers to mirror API shape for parity.

2026-03-14 - PM feedback (Evelyn Park): Add a short migration checklist for customers running Dedicated clusters (impact on connection density) and note recommended Dedicated capacity increases if switching to throughput preset.

2026-03-14 - Security note (Rajiv Menon): Ensure keepalive and connection lifetime changes do not degrade TLS session reuse visibility to KMS/HSM auditing. Marked security_review_required=true for final rollout planning.
